---
title: "optimise (M5_traits): budget allocation MILP using the chosen severe model"
output: html_document
---

This is a copy of `optimise.Rmd` that plans the extra $2M against the severe-incident model chosen in Part 1
(`M5_traits`, step 05), instead of refitting a separate Poisson GLM. See `optimise_m5traits_notes.md` for
what changed and why.

Run `part1/06_forecast.Rmd` first: this file reads its hand-off, `part1/forecast_fy2027.rds`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_dir("part1"))   # project root, wherever this is run from
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
if (interactive()) setwd(root)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ompr)
library(ompr.roi)
library(ROI)
library(ROI.plugin.glpk)
library(MASS)
select <- dplyr::select   # MASS masks select()
```

## 1. Model and baseline

> **In plain terms:** we start from Part 1's forecast of next year (FY2027) if nothing changes: about 21
> severe incidents. The model says how much each safety measure (lifeguards, drones, campaigns, flags,
> first aid, PA systems) lowers the risk. Those effects are what the money gets spent against.

Two things differ from `optimise.Rmd`:

-   **The model is the Part 1 choice.** Negative binomial, `offset(log(visitors))`, with season, weather, beach
    traits and visitor mix, refitted on all ten years in step 06. Lifeguard and drone hours enter as
    `log_lg = log1p(lg_hrs)` and `log_drone = log1p(drone_hrs)`: each *doubling* of hours has the same effect,
    so an hour is worth most where there are few.
-   **The baseline is the FY2027 forecast**, not last year's history. It uses step 06's assumed visitors and
    replayed weather, with safety inputs held at FY2026 levels. The safety terms add to the linear predictor
    and do not interact with weather, so multiplying the replay-averaged forecast by `exp(change)` is exact.

```{r data-model}
fc_obj <- readRDS("part1/forecast_fy2027.rds")
m_sev  <- fc_obj$final$sev
m_cc   <- fc_obj$final$cc     # same predictors; used only to report the knock-on effect on close calls

levers <- c(lg = "log_lg", dr = "log_drone", c = "campaign_idx", fa = "first_aid_cap", pa = "pa_system", fl = "flags")
b    <- setNames(coef(m_sev)[levers], names(levers))
b_cc <- setNames(coef(m_cc)[levers],  names(levers))

knitr::kable(cbind(coef = b, RR = exp(b), exp(confint.default(m_sev)[levers, ])), digits = 3,
             caption = "Safety levers in the severe model (RR < 1 = protective)")

# A lever with a coefficient >= 0 cannot reduce incidents, so it is switched off (never bought).
use <- b < 0
if (any(!use))
  message("Not bought (coefficient >= 0, no protective effect in the chosen model): ",
          paste(levers[!use], collapse = ", "))
b_eff <- ifelse(use, b, 0)   # the coefficients the optimiser plans against
```

The original GLM had `lg_hrs` with a *positive* coefficient (more lifeguards, more severe incidents) and a
large protective effect for first aid. Once visitors, season and beach hazard are in the model, the signs
come out the other way: lifeguards and drones are protective, and first aid and PA systems have no
measurable effect.

```{r window}
win <- fc_obj$forecast %>%
  arrange(beach_nm, month_date) %>%
  mutate(cal = as.integer(as.character(mon)))

stopifnot(all(table(win$beach_nm) == 12))

beach_ids <- unique(win$beach_nm)
pc_ids    <- sort(unique(win$postcode))

win <- win %>%
  mutate(
    r       = row_number(),
    b       = match(beach_nm, beach_ids),
    p       = match(postcode, pc_ids),
    mth_idx = rep(1:12, times = length(beach_ids))   # 1 = Sep 2026, 12 = Aug 2027
  )

win$mu0    <- win$mu_sev   # baseline expected severe incidents (step 06, weather replay)
win$mu0_cc <- win$mu_cc
baseline_total <- sum(win$mu0)

cat("Planning window:", format(min(win$month_date), "%b %Y"), "to", format(max(win$month_date), "%b %Y"), "\n")
cat("Baseline expected severe incidents (FY2027, no extra funding):", round(baseline_total, 2), "\n")
```

## 2. Prices and settings

> **In plain terms:** what each item costs, plus the practical rules we impose. Examples: no more
> lifeguard hours at a beach than the busiest beach has ever had; one drone flies at most 120 hours a
> month; and if we patrol a beach that currently has none, it is a real roster (at least 50 hours that
> month), not a single hour.

The minimum blocks are new. With `log1p(hours)`, going from 0 to 1 hour is a full log-unit, so the model
says one hour of patrol at an unpatrolled beach removes about 10% of its severe risk. That comes from the
curve's shape at zero, not from the data: no beach-month in ten years had between 1 and 48 lifeguard
hours (the smallest positive value is 49). Without a minimum, the optimiser would sprinkle one or two hours
over hundreds of winter beach-months. The blocks keep every purchase inside the range the data covers.

```{r prices}
prices <- read.csv("part1/pricing.csv")
price  <- function(x) prices$cost_fd[match(x, prices$item)]

BUDGET     <- 2e6
AMORT      <- 1      # years to spread one-off costs over (1 = full cash cost this year; drones have a 3-year life)
K          <- 8      # tangent lines per beach-month for exp() (the delta range is wider than before)
J          <- 8      # tangent lines per beach-month for each log1p(hours) curve
TIME_LIMIT <- 300    # solver time limit, seconds
MAX_FTE    <- 2      # max full-time lifeguards per beach
MAX_FA     <- 4      # max first-aid purchases per postcode
ACTIVE_SHARE <- 0.95 # only model the beach-months holding this share of the achievable gain

MIN_LG     <- 50     # min hours in a beach-month that currently has no patrol (smallest observed positive: 49)
MIN_DR     <- 5      # min drone hours in a beach-month that currently has none (smallest observed positive: 4)

DRONE_CAP  <- 120    # flight hours / month per drone
FTE_HRS    <- 1750   # lifeguard hours / FTE / year
FTE_H      <- FTE_HRS / 12
CAMP_LEVEL <- 0.7
SUMMER     <- c(11, 12, 1, 2)
FA_STEP    <- 10
FA_MAX     <- 100
PA_MAINT   <- 2000

c_lg      <- price("Casual SLSC lifeguard")
c_fte     <- price("Full-time SLSC lifeguard") + price("Full-time recruitment") / AMORT
c_dr_hr   <- price("Drone operator (casual)")
c_dr_buy  <- (price("Drone hardware") + price("Drone operator training")) / AMORT
c_camp    <- price("Beach safety education campaign")
c_fa      <- price("Community first aid & rescue training")
c_pa      <- price("PA system") / AMORT + PA_MAINT
c_fl      <- price("Rip-warning flags/signage") / AMORT
stopifnot(!anyNA(c(c_lg, c_fte, c_dr_hr, c_dr_buy, c_camp, c_fa, c_pa, c_fl)))
stopifnot(MIN_LG <= FTE_H)   # an FTE on its own always meets the minimum block
```

## 3. Precompute what each purchase can change

> **In plain terms:** for every beach and month, work out the most each measure could add (how many more
> hours fit, whether flags are already up, and so on) and how much risk that would remove. Months where
> nothing much can change are left out to keep the problem small.

```{r precompute}
N <- nrow(win); B <- length(beach_ids); P <- length(pc_ids)
bi  <- win$b
pci <- win$p

# Lifeguards: do not extrapolate past the most hours any beach-month has had
LG_CAP <- max(readRDS("part1/panel_f.rds")$lg_hrs)
lg0    <- win$lg_hrs
lg_room <- pmax(LG_CAP - lg0, 0)
lg_zero <- lg0 == 0

# Drones: existing equipment if the beach already flies in the baseline year
dr0     <- win$drone_hrs
have_b  <- as.numeric(tapply(dr0, bi, max) > 0)
dcap_b  <- pmax(DRONE_CAP, as.numeric(tapply(dr0, bi, max)))
room_dr <- ifelse(have_b[bi] == 1, pmax(dcap_b[bi] - dr0, 0), 0)
new_dr  <- ifelse(have_b[bi] == 1, 0, DRONE_CAP)
dr_max  <- room_dr + new_dr
dr_zero <- dr0 == 0

# Flags / PA: only rows where not already installed benefit
fl_mask <- as.numeric(win$flags == 0)
pa_mask <- as.numeric(win$pa_system == 0)

# Campaign: raises campaign_idx to at least 0.7 in Nov-Feb
camp_gain <- ifelse(win$cal %in% SUMMER, pmax(CAMP_LEVEL - win$campaign_idx, 0), 0)

# First aid: +10 per purchase, capped at 100, effective from the following month
fa_cap_w <- ifelse(win$mth_idx == 1, 0, pmax(FA_MAX - win$first_aid_cap, 0))

# Gain in log1p(hours) from adding x hours to h0
lgain <- function(h0, x) log1p(h0 + x) - log1p(h0)
g_lg_max <- lgain(lg0, lg_room)
g_dr_max <- lgain(dr0, dr_max)

# Most negative change in the linear predictor if every lever is maxed at this row
d_min <- b_eff[["lg"]] * g_lg_max + b_eff[["dr"]] * g_dr_max +
         b_eff[["fa"]] * fa_cap_w + b_eff[["fl"]] * fl_mask +
         b_eff[["pa"]] * pa_mask  + b_eff[["c"]]  * camp_gain

# Tangent lines for mu = mu0 * exp(delta)
d0  <- t(sapply(d_min, function(m) seq(m, 0, length.out = K)))
S   <- win$mu0 * exp(d0)
Cst <- S * (1 - d0)

# Tangent lines for the log1p gain, which is concave in hours: t <= g(x0) + g'(x0) (x - x0).
# x0 = 0 always (so t = 0 when nothing is bought), then a geometric grid from the minimum block
# (or 10 h) to the room available, since the curve bends most at small x.
log_grid <- function(h0, room, lo) {
  if (room <= 0) return(rep(0, J))
  lo <- min(lo, room)
  c(0, lo * (room / lo)^(seq(0, 1, length.out = J - 1)))
}
X_lg <- t(mapply(log_grid, lg0, lg_room, ifelse(lg_zero, MIN_LG, 10)))
X_dr <- t(mapply(log_grid, dr0, dr_max,  ifelse(dr_zero, MIN_DR, 5)))
tan_slope <- function(h0, X) 1 / (1 + h0 + X)                       # N x J
tan_int   <- function(h0, X) lgain(h0, X) - X / (1 + h0 + X)        # N x J
A_lg <- tan_slope(lg0, X_lg); I_lg <- tan_int(lg0, X_lg)
A_dr <- tan_slope(dr0, X_dr); I_dr <- tan_int(dr0, X_dr)

# Speed-up: only model beach-months that can actually shed incidents
pot <- win$mu0 * (1 - exp(d_min))
if (sum(pot) <= 0) stop("No lever can reduce incidents under this model (check coefficient signs).")
ord <- order(-pot)
act <- sort(ord[seq_len(which(cumsum(pot[ord]) / sum(pot) >= ACTIVE_SHARE)[1])])
isact <- as.numeric(seq_len(N) %in% act)
cat("Modelled beach-months:", length(act), "of", N, "\n")

need_fl   <- as.numeric(tapply(fl_mask * isact, bi, max)) * use[["fl"]]
need_pa   <- as.numeric(tapply(pa_mask * isact, bi, max)) * use[["pa"]]
need_camp <- as.numeric(tapply(camp_gain * isact, pci, max) > 0) * use[["c"]]
need_fa   <- as.numeric(tapply(fa_cap_w * isact, pci, max) > 0) * use[["fa"]]
have_act  <- as.numeric(tapply(isact, bi, max) > 0)
act_lgz   <- act[lg_zero[act]]          # modelled rows that need the lifeguard minimum block
act_drz   <- act[dr_zero[act]]          # ... and the drone minimum block
```

## 4. The MILP

> **In plain terms:** a solver tries every affordable mix of purchases and picks the one with the fewest
> expected severe incidents, within the $2M. The model's curves are replaced by straight-line pieces so
> the solver can handle them. The answer is then re-checked with the exact curves in section 5.

The objective is the sum of `mu0 * exp(delta)`, where
`delta = b_lg * t_lg + b_dr * t_dr + b_c * campaign + b_fl * flags + b_fa * first aid + b_pa * PA`.

-   `t_lg` and `t_dr` are the gains in `log1p(hours)`. They are concave in hours, and their coefficients are
    negative, so the solver wants them large. Capping each from above by `J` tangent lines lets it reach
    the curve but not go past it.
-   `exp(delta)` is convex, so `z >= mu0 * exp(delta)` is approximated from below by `K` tangent lines, as
    before.

Both approximations are slightly optimistic. On the other hand, beach-wide purchases (FTEs, flags,
campaigns) also help the months that were left out of the solver, and the solver does not count that. So
the MILP objective is only a guide, and section 5 recomputes the result exactly over all 960 beach-months.

```{r model}
model <- MIPModel() %>%
  # row-level (beach-month) variables
  add_variable(lg[r],  r = act, type = "continuous", lb = 0) %>%   # extra casual lifeguard hours
  add_variable(dh[r],  r = act, type = "continuous", lb = 0) %>%   # extra drone flight hours
  add_variable(tl[r],  r = act, type = "continuous", lb = 0) %>%   # gain in log1p(lifeguard hours)
  add_variable(td[r],  r = act, type = "continuous", lb = 0) %>%   # gain in log1p(drone hours)
  add_variable(w[r],   r = act, type = "continuous", lb = 0) %>%   # first-aid points in effect
  add_variable(z[r],   r = act, type = "continuous", lb = 0) %>%   # expected incidents (epigraph)
  add_variable(onl[r], r = act_lgz, type = "binary") %>%           # casual patrol switched on (unpatrolled rows)
  add_variable(ond[r], r = act_drz, type = "binary") %>%           # drone flying switched on (rows with no flights)
  # beach-level
  add_variable(fte[i],  i = 1:B, type = "integer", lb = 0, ub = MAX_FTE) %>%
  add_variable(ydr[i],  i = 1:B, type = "binary") %>%
  add_variable(flag[i], i = 1:B, type = "binary") %>%
  add_variable(pa[i],   i = 1:B, type = "binary") %>%
  # postcode-level
  add_variable(camp[j], j = 1:P, type = "binary") %>%
  add_variable(fa[j],   j = 1:P, type = "integer", lb = 0, ub = MAX_FA) %>%
  set_objective(sum_expr(z[r], r = act), "min") %>%
  # tangent-line approximation of mu0 * exp(delta)
  add_constraint(
    z[r] >= S[r, k] * (b_eff[["lg"]] * tl[r] + b_eff[["dr"]] * td[r] + b_eff[["fa"]] * w[r] +
                       b_eff[["fl"]] * fl_mask[r] * flag[bi[r]] +
                       b_eff[["pa"]] * pa_mask[r] * pa[bi[r]] +
                       b_eff[["c"]] * camp_gain[r] * camp[pci[r]]) + Cst[r, k],
    r = act, k = 1:K
  ) %>%
  # log1p gains, capped by tangent lines of the concave curve
  add_constraint(tl[r] <= A_lg[r, jj] * (lg[r] + FTE_H * fte[bi[r]]) + I_lg[r, jj], r = act, jj = 1:J) %>%
  add_constraint(td[r] <= A_dr[r, jj] * dh[r] + I_dr[r, jj], r = act, jj = 1:J) %>%
  add_constraint(tl[r] <= g_lg_max[r], r = act) %>%
  add_constraint(td[r] <= g_dr_max[r], r = act) %>%
  # physical limits
  add_constraint(lg[r] + FTE_H * fte[bi[r]] <= lg_room[r], r = act) %>%
  add_constraint(dh[r] <= room_dr[r] + new_dr[r] * ydr[bi[r]], r = act) %>%
  add_constraint(w[r] <= FA_STEP * fa[pci[r]], r = act) %>%
  add_constraint(w[r] <= fa_cap_w[r], r = act) %>%
  # minimum blocks where a beach-month currently has none (an FTE alone always clears MIN_LG)
  add_constraint(lg[r] <= lg_room[r] * onl[r], r = act_lgz) %>%
  add_constraint(lg[r] + FTE_H * fte[bi[r]] >= MIN_LG * onl[r], r = act_lgz) %>%
  add_constraint(dh[r] <= dr_max[r] * ond[r], r = act_drz) %>%
  add_constraint(dh[r] >= MIN_DR * ond[r], r = act_drz) %>%
  # only buy what can have an effect
  add_constraint(ydr[i]  <= (1 - have_b[i]) * have_act[i] * use[["dr"]], i = 1:B) %>%
  add_constraint(fte[i]  <= MAX_FTE * have_act[i] * use[["lg"]], i = 1:B) %>%
  add_constraint(flag[i] <= need_fl[i],    i = 1:B) %>%
  add_constraint(pa[i]   <= need_pa[i],    i = 1:B) %>%
  add_constraint(camp[j] <= need_camp[j],  j = 1:P) %>%
  add_constraint(fa[j]   <= MAX_FA * need_fa[j], j = 1:P) %>%
  # budget
  add_constraint(
    sum_expr(c_lg * lg[r] + c_dr_hr * dh[r], r = act) +
    sum_expr(c_fte * fte[i] + c_dr_buy * ydr[i] + c_fl * flag[i] + c_pa * pa[i], i = 1:B) +
    sum_expr(c_camp * camp[j] + c_fa * fa[j], j = 1:P) <= BUDGET
  )
```

```{r solve}
# HiGHS is far faster than GLPK here: install.packages("ROI.plugin.highs").
# (Its ROI plugin has no relative-gap option, so it solves to its default tolerance within TIME_LIMIT.)
if (requireNamespace("ROI.plugin.highs", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(ROI.plugin.highs)
  res <- solve_model(model, with_ROI(solver = "highs", control = list(time_limit = TIME_LIMIT)))
} else {
  message("ROI.plugin.highs not installed - falling back to GLPK (slower).")
  res <- solve_model(model, with_ROI(solver = "glpk", tm_limit = TIME_LIMIT * 1000))
}
# ompr reports "error" for any stop short of proven optimality, including the time limit. What matters is
# that a feasible plan was found and how far it can be from the best possible (the gap).
roi_out <- res$additional_solver_output$ROI
cat("Solver status:", res$status, "-", roi_out$status$msg$message, "\n")
if (!is.null(roi_out$message$info$mip_gap))
  cat(sprintf("MIP gap: %.3f%% (the plan is at most this far from optimal under the approximation)\n",
              100 * roi_out$message$info$mip_gap))
if (!is.finite(objective_value(res))) stop("No feasible plan found.")
```

On this data HiGHS reaches the 300-second limit with a gap of about 0.06%. The plan is effectively optimal,
and `ompr` labels it "error" only because optimality was not proven.

## 5. Results (recomputed exactly from the model)

> **In plain terms:** take the solver's shopping list, put it back into the real model (no straight-line
> shortcuts), and count how many severe incidents it avoids next year, what it costs, and where the money
> goes.

```{r results}
fill_rows <- function(df) { v <- numeric(N); v[df$r] <- df$value; v }
lg_v   <- fill_rows(get_solution(res, lg[r]))
dh_v   <- fill_rows(get_solution(res, dh[r]))
fte_v  <- get_solution(res, fte[i])  %>% arrange(i) %>% pull(value) %>% round()
ydr_v  <- get_solution(res, ydr[i])  %>% arrange(i) %>% pull(value) %>% round()
flag_v <- get_solution(res, flag[i]) %>% arrange(i) %>% pull(value) %>% round()
pa_v   <- get_solution(res, pa[i])   %>% arrange(i) %>% pull(value) %>% round()
camp_v <- get_solution(res, camp[j]) %>% arrange(j) %>% pull(value) %>% round()
fa_v   <- get_solution(res, fa[j])   %>% arrange(j) %>% pull(value) %>% round()

# Physical inputs actually in effect, then the exact change in the linear predictor
add_lg <- lg_v + FTE_H * fte_v[bi]
w_true <- pmin(FA_STEP * fa_v[pci], fa_cap_w)
X_eff <- cbind(lg = lgain(lg0, add_lg), dr = lgain(dr0, dh_v), c = camp_gain * camp_v[pci],
               fa = w_true, pa = pa_mask * pa_v[bi], fl = fl_mask * flag_v[bi])
d_eta    <- drop(X_eff %*% b[colnames(X_eff)])
d_eta_cc <- drop(X_eff %*% b_cc[colnames(X_eff)])

win$mu_new    <- win$mu0 * exp(d_eta)
win$mu_new_cc <- win$mu0_cc * exp(d_eta_cc)

cost <- c(
  casual_lifeguards = c_lg * sum(lg_v),
  full_time_lifeguards = c_fte * sum(fte_v),
  drone_hours = c_dr_hr * sum(dh_v),
  drone_hardware_training = c_dr_buy * sum(ydr_v),
  campaigns = c_camp * sum(camp_v),
  first_aid = c_fa * sum(fa_v),
  pa_systems = c_pa * sum(pa_v),
  flags = c_fl * sum(flag_v)
)
stopifnot(sum(cost) <= BUDGET + 1)

avoided <- baseline_total - sum(win$mu_new)
cat(sprintf("Spent %s of %s\n", format(round(sum(cost)), big.mark = ","), format(BUDGET, big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Expected severe incidents FY2027: %.1f -> %.1f  (%.1f avoided, %.1f%%)\n",
            baseline_total, sum(win$mu_new), avoided, 100 * avoided / baseline_total))
cat(sprintf("Expected close calls FY2027:      %.1f -> %.1f  (knock-on, not optimised for)\n",
            sum(win$mu0_cc), sum(win$mu_new_cc)))
cat(sprintf("MILP objective (approximation; ignores gains in unmodelled months): %.2f\n",
            sum(get_solution(res, z[r])$value) + sum(win$mu0[-act])))
cat(sprintf("Cost per severe incident avoided: $%s\n", format(round(sum(cost) / avoided), big.mark = ",")))
print(round(cost))
```

### Which purchases do the work

> **In plain terms:** the total saving split by type of purchase. Each line is that purchase type on its
> own with everything else switched off, so the lines need not add up to the total (the effects multiply).

```{r attribution}
attr_tab <- sapply(colnames(X_eff), function(k) {
  d <- X_eff[, k] * b[[k]]
  baseline_total - sum(win$mu0 * exp(d))
})
spend_by_lever <- c(lg = sum(cost[c("casual_lifeguards", "full_time_lifeguards")]),
                    dr = sum(cost[c("drone_hours", "drone_hardware_training")]),
                    c = cost[["campaigns"]], fa = cost[["first_aid"]],
                    pa = cost[["pa_systems"]], fl = cost[["flags"]])
lever_tab <- tibble(lever = c(lg = "Lifeguards", dr = "Drones", c = "Campaigns", fa = "First aid",
                              pa = "PA systems", fl = "Flags/signage")[names(attr_tab)],
                    spend = spend_by_lever[names(attr_tab)],
                    severe_avoided_alone = attr_tab) %>%
  mutate(cost_per_incident = ifelse(severe_avoided_alone > 0, spend / severe_avoided_alone, NA)) %>%
  filter(spend > 0)
knitr::kable(lever_tab, digits = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
```

### How sure are we

> **In plain terms:** the effect sizes are estimates. We redraw them 2,000 times within their margin of
> error and recount the incidents avoided by the same plan, which gives a range instead of a single number.

```{r uncertainty}
set.seed(2027)
draws <- mvrnorm(2000, coef(m_sev)[levers], vcov(m_sev)[levers, levers])
colnames(draws) <- names(levers)
avoided_draws <- apply(draws, 1, function(bb)
  baseline_total - sum(win$mu0 * exp(drop(X_eff %*% bb[colnames(X_eff)]))))
round(c(point = avoided, quantile(avoided_draws, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))), 1)
```

This range covers only the uncertainty in the effect sizes. It leaves out the causal caveat (the effects
are associations; see the notes file) and the year-to-year chance in severe counts (step 06, section 5).

### Allocation

> **In plain terms:** the shopping list by beach and by postcode, with each beach's expected severe
> incidents before and after.

```{r allocation}
mon_lab <- function(rows) paste(month.abb[win$cal[rows]], collapse = " ")
by_beach <- tibble(
  beach = beach_ids,
  postcode = win %>% group_by(b) %>% summarise(p = first(postcode)) %>% pull(p),
  casual_lg_hrs = as.numeric(tapply(lg_v, bi, sum)),
  casual_months = sapply(seq_len(B), function(i) mon_lab(which(bi == i & lg_v > 0.5))),
  fte = fte_v, drone_bought = ydr_v, drone_hrs = as.numeric(tapply(dh_v, bi, sum)),
  flags = flag_v, pa = pa_v,
  expected_before = as.numeric(tapply(win$mu0, bi, sum)),
  expected_after  = as.numeric(tapply(win$mu_new, bi, sum))
) %>%
  mutate(avoided = expected_before - expected_after) %>%
  filter(casual_lg_hrs > 0.5 | fte > 0 | drone_bought > 0 | drone_hrs > 0.5 | flags > 0 | pa > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(avoided))

by_postcode <- tibble(postcode = pc_ids, campaign = camp_v, first_aid_purchases = fa_v) %>%
  filter(campaign > 0 | first_aid_purchases > 0)

by_month <- win %>% group_by(cal) %>%
  summarise(before = sum(mu0), after = sum(mu_new), casual_lg_hrs = sum(lg_v[r]), drone_hrs = sum(dh_v[r])) %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month.abb[cal], levels = month.abb[c(9:12, 1:8)])) %>%
  arrange(month) %>% select(month, everything(), -cal)

knitr::kable(by_beach, digits = 2)
knitr::kable(by_postcode)
knitr::kable(by_month, digits = 2)

write.csv(by_beach, "part2/optimal_allocation_m5_by_beach.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(by_postcode, "part2/optimal_allocation_m5_by_postcode.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
